dynamicwaters.configuration.rainCurrentB: How much faster the rivers run in the rain, as a share of their speed (0.25 = a quarter faster), growing as the rain sets in. Only where it rains, not where it snows or never rains.
dynamicwaters.configuration.stormCurrent: How much faster the rivers run in a thunderstorm, as a share of their speed (0.5 = half as fast again).
dynamicwaters.configuration.enableRiverF: Foam drifting down the rivers out to 48 blocks, more in fast water, churned up in rapids and thrown out where a waterfall lands.
dynamicwaters.configuration.enableRiverM: A mist of spray at the foot of every waterfall, faint spray off a bank the current runs into, and where foam is dashed against a bank or goes over the lip of a fall.
dynamicwaters.configuration.riverWaterCo: The rivers' own water colour: mountain rivers clear and green-blue, lowland rivers and deltas a little murky (both set in Water colours below), blended into the biomes' water like any biome's. Lakes and the sea keep theirs. The world is drawn again when you leave the menu.
dynamicwaters.configuration.mountainRive: The colour mountain rivers' water is taken toward, as #RRGGBB (River Water Colour on). Red while it is not a colour.
dynamicwaters.configuration.lowlandRiver: The colour lowland rivers' and deltas' water is taken toward, as #RRGGBB (River Water Colour on). Red while it is not a colour.
dynamicwaters.configuration.biomeWaterCo: Your own water colour for a biome, or every biome in a tag, in place of its own and the rivers': modid:biome=#RRGGBB or #modid:tag=#RRGGBB, with commas between. Example: minecraft:swamp=#4C6559, #minecraft:is_river=#3A8FC0. Red while one is not right.
dynamicwaters.reload.done: Dynamic Waters: the riverbank palettes and water plant sets were read again from their files (the config file is read by itself). To regenerate the land around you with the current settings, choose how many chunks around you: /dynamicwaters reload <radius in chunks, 1-16> - e.g. /dynamicwaters reload 2 regenerates 5x5 chunks with yours in the middle.
dynamicwaters.reload.warning: This regenerates %1$sx%1$s chunks with yours in the middle (%2$s chunks each way, %3$s in all) with the current settings. Everything built there will be lost, and the world may freeze for a while - the larger the radius, the longer. Are you sure?
dynamicwaters.reload.confirm.hover: Click (or run the same command again) within 30 seconds to regenerate
dynamicwaters.reload.regenerated: Dynamic Waters: regenerated %1$sx%1$s chunks around you, %2$s blocks changed, in %3$s s.
dynamicwaters.locate.overworld: Dynamic Waters' rivers only run in the Overworld.
dynamicwaters.locate.found: The nearest %s is at %s (%s blocks away)
dynamicwaters.configuration.muddyRainRiv: Rivers run muddy in the rain, browner in a thunderstorm, and clear again a while after it - only where it rains, not where it snows or never rains.
dynamicwaters.configuration.builtInWater: Water colours Dynamic Waters brings for the biomes of Regions Unexplored, Oh The Biomes We've Gone and Terralith: murky in the bogs and bayous, turquoise in the tropics, cold blue in the north. Used only while that mod is installed. Your own colour for a biome or tag goes before them.
dynamicwaters.configuration.riverFords.t: Now and then a lowland river runs shallow across - a block of water - with round boulders across it and room for a boat between them, and often a log sunk on the bed beside them. New chunks only.
dynamicwaters.configuration.oxbowLakes.t: Old bends a lowland river has cut itself off from: a still crescent of water beside the river, on the outside of a bend, with reeds and lily pads. Only on low, flat land. New chunks only.
dynamicwaters.configuration.clearRiverWa: Under a river's water you see far at once. Minecraft's underwater fog, which closes in to a few blocks as you go under and clears only slowly, is pushed out to the render distance. Lakes and the sea keep it.
dynamicwaters.configuration.riverParticl: How often foam (and the old bubbles, if on) appears on rivers. Higher = FEWER.
dynamicwaters.configuration.oldRiverPart: The old bubbles on rivers, and puffs of cloud in rapids while the foam is off.
dynamicwaters.configuration.lakeBiome.to: The lakes' water gets the river biome (the frozen river biome in cold land): it shows in the weather, the mobs, the water colour and the F3 screen. Shores and plants stay those of the land round the lake. New chunks only.
dynamicwaters.gui.title: Dynamic Waters
dynamicwaters.gui.subtitle1: Rivers that flow, lakes that fill, water that moves.
dynamicwaters.gui.subtitle2: Pick a category. Changes save as you make them.
dynamicwaters.gui.fullEditor.tooltip: NeoForge's generated editor: every option, including lists (custom entity speeds, biome blacklist).
dynamicwaters.gui.worldgenNote: Affects newly generated terrain only. Existing chunks keep what they have.
dynamicwaters.gui.category.lowlandRivers: The long rivers: Dynamic Waters' own, Minecraft's own, or none.
dynamicwaters.gui.category.mountainRiver: Streams that follow the terrain's real drainage down to the lowland rivers and the sea.
dynamicwaters.gui.category.lowlandTunnel: Lowland rivers running under high ground in closed tunnels instead of open gorges.
dynamicwaters.gui.category.mountainTunne: Mountain rivers going into the hillsides and coming out further down.
dynamicwaters.gui.category.lakes.desc: Natural basins in the mountains filled to their rim, at whatever height they sit.
dynamicwaters.gui.category.waterside.des: How the rivers and lakes look: what they lay on their banks and beds, what grows in and along the water, the boulders in the current.
dynamicwaters.gui.category.flow.desc: How hard the current pushes players, mobs, items and ships, and how rain changes it.
dynamicwaters.gui.category.visuals.desc: Flowing water texture, particles, water colours, ice floes, ambient sound, and the main-menu extras.
dynamicwaters.gui.category.general.desc: Welcome message and compatibility switches for other terrain mods.
dynamicwaters.configuration.mountainTunn: How often a mountain river goes into a hillside, on slopes with room for a tunnel. Often = wherever the ground has room for one. New chunks only.
Longest a river runs level through the rock, in blocks, before its way in. The tunnel ends sooner where the ground lets it. New chunks only.
How far under its old level a river goes in a tunnel, in blocks. Deeper = more rock over it and longer tunnels, on steeper ground. New chunks only.
Height of a tunnel's roof over the water, in blocks. A wide river's tunnel is taller than this. New chunks only.
Width of the dry ledge along each side of the water, in blocks. New chunks only.
dynamicwaters.configuration.waterfallCav: Now and then a hollow in the rock behind a tall waterfall: a ledge over the pool below it, reached through the falling water. New chunks only.
dynamicwaters.gui.banks.label: Riverbank palettes
dynamicwaters.gui.banks.button.tooltip: What rivers and lakes lay on the ground they cut - beds sorted by the current, shores, bars - in spots, per biome, with a live preview.
dynamicwaters.gui.banks.title: Riverbank palettes
dynamicwaters.gui.banks.subtitle: What rivers and lakes lay on their beds and shores
dynamicwaters.gui.banks.edit.builtInTip: A built-in palette: saving it makes your own copy, which then replaces it.
dynamicwaters.gui.banks.delete.restoresT: The built-in palette of the same name comes back.
dynamicwaters.gui.banks.openFolder.toolt: config/dynamicwaters/riverbanks - your palette files, a README and examples of every built-in one.
dynamicwaters.gui.banks.name: Name
dynamicwaters.gui.banks.name.tooltip: The file name: lowercase letters, digits, _ and - only.
dynamicwaters.gui.banks.biomes.tooltip: Use this palette in these biomes (comma-separated). A palette naming the biome wins over any that fits by tag.
dynamicwaters.gui.banks.tags.tooltip: ...or in any biome that has ANY of these tags; of several palettes that fit by tag, the first in the list wins. Leave biomes and tags empty for the default palette.
dynamicwaters.gui.banks.not.tooltip: Never use this palette in these biomes, nor in a biome with any of these #tags.
dynamicwaters.gui.banks.place.rapids.des: The bed where the water runs hard: falls, steep streams, the middle of a river. Pebbles, cobbles, boulders.
dynamicwaters.gui.banks.place.silt.desc: The bed where the water slackens: lakes, deep pools, the edges of a river, delta channels. Sand, clay, mud.
dynamicwaters.gui.banks.place.shore.desc: The wet margin: the first block or two over the water, its top wavering along the water.
dynamicwaters.gui.banks.place.slope.desc: Cut ground above the shore. Empty: it keeps its own ground (the built-in palettes leave it so).
dynamicwaters.gui.banks.place.bars.desc: The shelves inside the bends, where they break the surface. Empty: the silt's blocks.
dynamicwaters.gui.banks.place.flats.desc: A delta's low land between its channels, along the water. Empty: the bars' blocks.
dynamicwaters.gui.banks.previewMode.tool: Which water the preview shows: each runs at its own strength, and sorts its bed its own way.
dynamicwaters.gui.banks.reroll.tooltip: Cut the section somewhere else: another stretch of the same water.
dynamicwaters.gui.banks.patch.tooltip: How wide a spot is, in blocks; 1 = block by block. The heaviest block of a list is the ground, the others lie on it in spots. Rapids break finer, silt and flats spread wider.
dynamicwaters.gui.banks.shoreHeight.tool: How many blocks over the water the shore reaches, give or take one along the water.
dynamicwaters.gui.banks.styleSwitch.tool: Off: where this palette applies, the cut ground is left as it is.
dynamicwaters.gui.banks.saveCopy.tooltip: Writes your own copy to the config folder; it replaces the built-in palette.
dynamicwaters.gui.banks.badName: Name: lowercase letters, digits, _ and - only.
dynamicwaters.gui.banks.emptyPlace: No blocks: this place keeps its ground.
dynamicwaters.gui.banks.emptyBars: No blocks: the silt's blocks are used.
dynamicwaters.gui.banks.emptyFlats: No blocks: the bars' blocks are used.

dynamicwaters.gui.plants.button.tooltip: What grows in and along the rivers and lakes - kelp, seagrass, lily pads, reeds, sea pickles - a list for the lowland rivers, one for the mountain rivers and one for the lakes, per biome.
dynamicwaters.gui.bankRules.label: Bank plants & bushes
dynamicwaters.gui.bankRules.button.toolt: Which plants grow on the bank's top behind a river's shore, and what leaves its bushes are of - per kind of land or biome, any mod's plants and leaves.
dynamicwaters.gui.bankRules.title: Bank plants & bushes
dynamicwaters.gui.bankRules.subtitle: The first rule whose lands fit a biome is the one used there
dynamicwaters.gui.bankRules.tab.plants.t: Grass, ferns, flowers: which plants grow on the bank's top, and how many of each.
dynamicwaters.gui.bankRules.tab.leaves.t: What leaves the bushes on the bank's top are of: the biome's own trees', none, or leaves you choose.
dynamicwaters.gui.bankRules.new.tooltip: A new rule at the end of the list. Move it up to have it tried before the others.
dynamicwaters.gui.bankRules.up: Up the list: tried before the rule above it
dynamicwaters.gui.bankRules.down: Down the list: tried after the rule below it
dynamicwaters.gui.bankRules.reset.toolti: This list's rules back to the mod's own.
dynamicwaters.gui.bankRules.resetConfirm: Reset this list to the defaults?
dynamicwaters.gui.bankRules.emptyPlants: No rules: no plants grow on the banks.
dynamicwaters.gui.bankRules.emptyLeaves: No rules: no bushes grow on the banks.
dynamicwaters.gui.bankRules.nowhere.warn: This rule is for no land: it is never used. Pick a kind of land or a biome.
dynamicwaters.gui.bankRules.unused.warn: Rules above this one take all its biomes in this world: here it is never used.
dynamicwaters.gui.bankRules.noWorld: Open this in a world to see the biomes the rule is used in.
dynamicwaters.gui.bankRules.land.any.des: Every biome: a rule for everything the rules above it leave.
Wooded temperate land: forests, taigas, groves - any mod's.
dynamicwaters.gui.bankRules.land.grassla: Open temperate land: plains, meadows, fields.
dynamicwaters.gui.bankRules.land.lush.de: Jungles, swamps and other lush land.
dynamicwaters.gui.bankRules.land.cold.de: Land where it snows: snowy plains, tundras, snowy taigas.
dynamicwaters.gui.bankRules.land.dry.des: Savannas, shrublands and other dry land.
dynamicwaters.gui.bankRules.land.beach.d: Beaches, where a river meets the sea.
dynamicwaters.gui.bankRules.biomes.toolt: Also for these biomes (comma-separated): a biome's id, a #tag of biomes, or a mod's id with * for all its biomes.
dynamicwaters.gui.bankRules.addBiome.too: Pick a biome or a tag of biomes from this world's.
Another plant in this one's place.
dynamicwaters.gui.bankRules.weight.toolt: How many of this plant, against the others: a plant of weight 10 grows ten times as often as one of weight 1. How many bank blocks get a plant at all: Riverbank Plant Density.
dynamicwaters.gui.bankRules.mode.auto.de: The leaves of the trees the biome itself grows, worked out from its trees - any mod's biomes and trees alike. Bushes only in wooded land.
dynamicwaters.gui.bankRules.mode.block.d: Bushes of the leaves you choose, any mod's - in open land too, there a little fewer.
dynamicwaters.gui.bankRules.needPlant: Add at least one plant with a weight over 0.
dynamicwaters.gui.bankRules.badLeaves: No such block: choose the leaves again.

dynamicwaters.gui.waterColors.noWorld: Open a world to pick from its biomes - or type the name.

dynamicwaters.gui.plants.name.tooltip: The file's name: lowercase letters, digits, _ and - only.
dynamicwaters.gui.plants.biomes.tooltip: Use this set in these biomes (comma-separated). A set that names a biome wins over any matched by tags.
dynamicwaters.gui.plants.tags.tooltip: ...or in every biome with ANY of these tags; of several sets that match by tags, the first in the list wins. No biomes and no tags = the default set.

dynamicwaters.gui.plants.kind.lowland.de: The lowland (2D) rivers and their deltas.
dynamicwaters.gui.plants.kind.mountain.d: The mountain (3D) rivers and streams, their pools and ravines.
dynamicwaters.gui.plants.moveUp: Up the list: tried before the one above it
dynamicwaters.gui.plants.changeBlock.too: Pick another block for this plant; its settings stay.
dynamicwaters.gui.plants.at.bed.desc: On the bottom, under the water: seagrass, kelp, sea pickles, corals.
dynamicwaters.gui.plants.at.surface.desc: On top of still water, open to the sky: lily pads. Never where it snows.
dynamicwaters.gui.plants.at.shore.desc: On dirt or sand beside the water, at its level: reeds. Never where it snows.
dynamicwaters.gui.plants.chance.tooltip: Of the places this plant could grow - or, in patches, of a patch's: 100% everywhere, 1 in 500 once in 500 places.
dynamicwaters.gui.plants.depth.tooltip: How many blocks of water over the bed, from and to. On the water: the water under it.
dynamicwaters.gui.plants.calm.tooltip: Only where the water is calm: a lake, a river's slack margins, a delta, a mountain river where it hardly falls.
dynamicwaters.gui.plants.alone.tooltip: Never next to another of it: one here, one there.
dynamicwaters.gui.plants.patch.tooltip: Grows only in patches about this many blocks across, like a kelp bed; off = anywhere.
dynamicwaters.gui.plants.patchShare.tool: How much of the water the patches cover. The chance is then how thick a patch is.
dynamicwaters.gui.plants.height.tooltip: How many blocks tall, for a plant that stacks: reeds. Kelp grows toward the surface on its own.
dynamicwaters.gui.plants.setSwitch.toolt: Off: nothing grows in the waters this set is for.
dynamicwaters.gui.plants.saveCopy.toolti: Saves your copy in the config folder; it replaces the built-in set.
dynamicwaters.gui.plants.empty: No plants in this water - add one.
dynamicwaters.gui.plants.hint: The list is tried from the top: the first plant that can grow at a place takes it. One set per biome - a set for some biomes lists everything that grows there. New chunks only.
dynamicwaters.configuration.title: Dynamic Waters Configuration
dynamicwaters.configuration.normalRiverD: How many lowland rivers a world gets, against the default (High): Very Low about 1/9, Low about 4/9, Medium about 2/3, Ultra about 1.8x, Extreme about 2.8x, Insane about 7x.
dynamicwaters.configuration.riverBiomeCh: How likely rivers are in a biome, lowland and mountain rivers alike: each entry "<biomes> <chance>", the first that matches used. Biomes: an id (minecraft:desert), a tag after # (#minecraft:is_badlands) or an id ending in * (terralith:*), several apart by spaces; chance 0 to 1, 1 = as anywhere, 0 = none. E.g. "minecraft:desert 0.2". New chunks only.
dynamicwaters.configuration.mountainRive: How many mountain rivers a world gets. A stream starts wherever enough terrain drains into one spot; each step down roughly halves the streams. Very Low = only the largest valleys carry a river, High = default, Insane = a dense network of small streams.
dynamicwaters.configuration.normalTunnel: Height of a tunnel's roof over the water at its middle, in blocks, give or take a few. New chunks only.
Width of a dry ledge along each side of the water, in blocks. 0 = the water reaches the walls. New chunks only.
Rare single pillars of rock standing in a tunnel. New chunks only.
Rock rising from the bed and hanging from the roof, as in a cave. New chunks only.
Now and then a natural rock arch over a river running between high rock walls, of the walls' own rock, the river running free under it. New chunks only.
dynamicwaters.configuration.riverBoulder: Rounded boulders in the lowland rivers, along their shallows, and very rarely a rock in a mountain stream's rapids. New chunks only.
dynamicwaters.configuration.mountainRive: How mountain rivers freeze in cold land. Never = none of their running water freezes. Calm stretches = they freeze like still water, but waterfalls and rapids stay open so the falling water does not run out over the ice. Fully frozen = waterfalls and rapids freeze too and stop running. Lakes, the sea and the frozen lowland rivers freeze either way.
dynamicwaters.configuration.lowlandRiver: How wide the lowland rivers are: 1.0 = default, 0.5 = half as wide, 2.0 = twice as wide. NEW WORLDS ONLY: a world keeps the width it was created with, and older worlds keep 1.0.

How deep the lowland rivers are: 1.0 = default, 0.5 = half as deep, 2.0 = twice as deep. Lakes stay deeper than the rivers. NEW WORLDS ONLY: a world keeps the depth it was created with, and older worlds keep 1.0.
dynamicwaters.configuration.mountainRive: How wide the mountain rivers are: 1.0 = default, 0.5 = half as wide, 2.0 = twice as wide. A wider river is also a little deeper. NEW WORLDS ONLY: a world keeps the width it was created with, and older worlds keep 1.0.

How deep the mountain rivers are: 1.0 = default, 0.5 = half as deep, 2.0 = twice as deep. Lakes stay deeper than the rivers. NEW WORLDS ONLY: a world keeps the depth it was created with, and older worlds keep 1.0.
dynamicwaters.configuration.lowlandRiver: How a lowland river is cut into higher ground. Gorge = steep banks, and a gorge's walls where the ground is high, as before. Valley = a wide, smooth valley: a strip of flat ground at the water, slopes rising gently; where the hills are higher still the slope goes on up steeper, as a gorge's wall. The mixed cuts (Valley + Gorge, Gorge + Tunnel, Valley + Gorge + Tunnel) use each where Cut Chosen By puts it, changing gradually along the river; a tunnel runs closed under the ground. The two with a tunnel are experimental. Only with lowland tunnels off. NEW WORLDS ONLY: a world keeps the cut it was created with, and older worlds keep Gorge.

For the mixed cuts: what chooses the cut along a river. Height = how high the ground stands over the river: a valley under Valley Below, a tunnel over Tunnel Above, a gorge between. Biome = the land's biome along the river: a valley in the valley biomes, a tunnel in the tunnel biomes, a gorge elsewhere (both lists are in the full config file). NEW WORLDS ONLY.
dynamicwaters.configuration.lowlandValle: With the cut chosen by height: a valley where the ground over the river stands under this Y, a gorge (or a tunnel) where it is higher. NEW WORLDS ONLY.
dynamicwaters.configuration.lowlandTunne: With the cut chosen by height: a tunnel where the ground over the river stands over this Y. NEW WORLDS ONLY.
dynamicwaters.configuration.lowlandValle: With the cut chosen by biome: the biomes a lowland river runs through in a valley. A biome id (minecraft:plains), a tag after # (#minecraft:is_forest), or an id ending in * (terralith:*). NEW WORLDS ONLY.
dynamicwaters.configuration.lowlandTunne: With the cut chosen by biome: the biomes a lowland river runs through in a tunnel, written as the valley biomes. NEW WORLDS ONLY.
dynamicwaters.configuration.riverbankPla: On the bank's top behind a river's shore: grass, tall grass, ferns and flowers by the biome, and in wooded land bushes of its trees' leaves; sugar cane at the water, small dripleaf in the shallows. Only with River Shores on. New chunks only.
How thickly the riverbank plants grow: 1.0 = default, 0.5 = half as many, 2.0 = twice as many (as far as there is room). New chunks only.
dynamicwaters.configuration.riverbankOwn: The bank's top also grows other mods' grasses, ferns and flowers a biome grows (found in what the biome generates), in the share the biome has them: other mods' biomes, and vanilla ones those mods add plants to. Without other mods nothing changes. New chunks only.
dynamicwaters.configuration.riverbankPla: Which plants grow on the bank's top, by the land: "<lands> -> <plant> <weight>, ...", the first entry whose lands match used. Lands: biome ids, #tags, ids ending in *, * for any, or @forest @grassland @lush @cold @dry @desert @badlands @beach. Any mod's plants. New chunks only.
dynamicwaters.configuration.riverbankBus: The leaves of the bushes on the bank's top: "<lands> -> <leaves | auto | none>", the first entry whose lands match used. auto = the leaves of the biome's own trees, any mod's biomes and trees alike. New chunks only.
dynamicwaters.configuration.raggedShores: How often a lowland river's shore breaks up for a stretch into tufts of grass and earth with puddles and runnels of the river's water between them, in temperate land. Only with River Shores on. New chunks only.
dynamicwaters.configuration.gravelBarBio: The biomes where a lowland river's islands are gravel bars - low, flat and all gravel, no trees - and where it divides round them more often. Elsewhere its islands are of the land, trees and all. A biome id (minecraft:plains), a tag after # (#minecraft:is_forest), or an id ending in * (terralith:*). Empty = no gravel bars. New chunks only.
dynamicwaters.configuration.riverBeaches: A strip of shore along the lowland rivers and round their islands: a block or two of ground at the water's level and the bed just under it, by the biome: podzol and coarse dirt with cobbles at the water in a wood, gravel and clay on grassland (the whole bed gravel), sand on a beach, red sand and terracotta in the badlands, sand in a desert. The gently running stretches of the mountain rivers get the same on their banks. New chunks only.
How often a lowland river divides for a stretch: its water runs in two or three arms round low islands, then comes together again. On open grassland more often, round gravel bars (with River Shores on). New chunks only.
dynamicwaters.configuration.riverFallenL: How often a fallen trunk lies over the water between a river's islands, of the wood of the trees around it. Needs River Islands on and Lowland River Tunnels off. New chunks only.
dynamicwaters.configuration.mountainRive: Give the middle of a mountain river the river biome (frozen river in cold land). Banks, beds and plants stay those of the land round the river. Only with dynamic lowland rivers. New chunks only.
dynamicwaters.configuration.seasonalIceF: With Serene Seasons: from early to late winter, ice floes come down every river, lowland or mountain, in any land with a winter - not in deserts nor in tropical biomes. None in spring. As often as Ice Floes has them.
dynamicwaters.configuration.riverIceFloe: How often a group of thin ice floes comes floating down a mountain river's open water in cold land, carried by the current - over a waterfall they drop - until they crack apart a few minutes later, the small ones first. A blow breaks one; a player goes through it into the water.
dynamicwaters.configuration.deltaInlandR: How far inland a big lowland river's delta may begin, in blocks up the river from the coast. Lower = deltas nearer the coast. 0 = no deltas at all; under 90 counts as 90; 512 = as far as the river's size allows. New chunks only - best set before creating a world.
dynamicwaters.configuration.realisticCur: Rivers run fastest down the middle and at the surface, slow along the banks and by the bed, faster round the outside of a bend than inside it; mountain rivers faster the steeper they fall, lowland rivers lazier the broader they are, and faster where they narrow. The water pushes you, boats and items as the square of its speed: fast water sweeps things along, slack water by the banks barely moves them. Off = the same current all across and all along every river.
A river carries its current on into the lake or sea it runs into, spreading and fading out over a few dozen blocks, and a lake's water is drawn into the river that leaves it. Off = the current stops dead where the river meets still water.
dynamicwaters.configuration.waterfallCur: The water speeds up toward the edge of a waterfall, the falling water pulls you down it, and in the pool at its foot the water boils out away from the fall while eddies along the banks run back toward it, so floating things go round there.
dynamicwaters.configuration.currentWobbl: Now and then the current in the fastest water - rapids, steep mountain reaches - swings a little from side to side and surges, so a boat there sways.
dynamicwaters.configuration.livingCurren: The rivers' current follows what you build in the water and dig out of the banks: it stands still before a dam and for a stretch below it, runs round a pier and faster through a narrowing, and down a canal that leads back into the river. The water's level never changes.
